column4: Visit note | 2026-06-29 10:00 AM | Dr. Selina Parvin, Neurology | Patient: Karim Chowdhury, 48, male. Mr. Chowdhury reports feeling waves of nausea alongside a sensation of the room spinning, dizziness whenever he looks up, and a brief spinning feeling when he turns over in bed. He is a CNG auto-rickshaw driver and mentions the trouble began after bumping his head on a rickshaw hood in Shyamoli. He denies any hearing loss, ringing in the ears, numbness, or fainting episodes. On examination: Dix-Hallpike test positive on the right side, BP 136/80 mmHg, pulse 91 bpm, weight 91 kg. Cranial nerves are intact and coordination is normal. Assessment: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to get up slowly from bed, avoid sudden head movements, and repeat the Epley manoeuvre at home as shown. Follow-up in 2 weeks.
